newsitem.title: UK: Entergy details London bid rationale.
newsitem.headline: Entergy details London bid rationale.

text.p: U.S. power group Entergy Corp on Wednesday detailed the rationale behind its 1.267 billion stg agreed cash offer for UK regional electricity company London Electricity.

In a statement the company said the offer by its UK subsidiary Entergy Power UK Plc would "create a partnership through which both companies can pool expertise and working practices to further improve operating efficiencies".
Entergy said the recommended offer of 705 pence, with a loan note alternative, would also enable it to "gain experience for the development of its U.S. business after deregulation".
Entergy also said buying London Electricity would provide it with the basis for "developing an expanded business in the UK" and "provide a platform for...future expansions in Europe".

It said the acquisition would reinforce London Electricity's focus on "providing a high quality service to its customers". This factor was underlined by London Electricity's chairman Sir Bob Reid in the same statement, who said it would help develop its "strong business base and its focus on customer service".
Reid said he was satisfied Entergy's assurances "given in relation to employees and their development are sound and...the relationship will provide wider opportunities for employees".
He said the London Electricity board unanimously recommended shareholders to accept the offer, which represented fair value and was in the best interests of shareholders, customers and employees.

Reid also said he was pleased Entergy's chairman had made a commitment to "the continuing reinforcement of the network to ensure the high standards of service to which London has become accustomed". An assurance "that the necessary capital investment will be made to meet the improved system performance standards agreed with the regulator and the growth requirements of London" was particularly important, he added.
